tier_reason: arXiv:2302.08417 is a preprint by the fork's own author (with BLIS maintainers); no peer-reviewed venue found, and compiler flags are unstated, so it is first-party evidence with partial methodology. It compares against OpenBLAS, MKL, AOCL and ArmPL with plots only, no numeric ratios.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Qualitative only (plots): outperforms OpenBLAS and conventional BLIS on Epyc 7R32 and matches AOCL there; highest throughput and consistency of all tested libraries on Graviton 3 (vs ArmPL, OpenBLAS); only MKL on Xeon E5-2690 beats it. No numeric ratios on page.
corrections.caveats: Evidence is an arXiv preprint (not peer-reviewed as far as found) by the fork's author; compiler flags unstated; no numeric ratios; MKL not beaten on Intel; fork with 1 star; GEMMFIP lives on the 'gemmfip' branch and is enabled with ./configure -s gemmfip; README does not document it.

notes: Record called the paper peer-reviewed (ACM); I found only the arXiv preprint (v2) and a BLIS Retreat 2023 talk. Last commit date 2023-04-26 not verified (GitHub commits page blocked by robots.txt). License BSD-3-Clause and fork-of flame/blis confirmed.

tier_reason: Peer-reviewed SC'21-era ACM paper comparing against OpenBLAS, BLIS, ARMPL, LIBXSMM and BLASFEO with GCC 8.2.1 -O3 on named ARM CPUs. Not A because the repo's benchmark directory times LibShalom only, not the baselines. Downgraded because the record's claim was overstated: the 2x and 2.6x figures are against other baselines, not OpenBLAS.

corrections.claimed_speedup: 2x higher throughput than BLASFEO at M=N=K=8 single-thread on Phytium 2000+; 2.6x higher GFLOPS than BLIS at M=32,N=50176,K=5000 on Phytium 2000+; 1.05-2x higher throughput than competing libraries overall; average 1.8x over the second-best (BLIS) on irregular shapes

notes: The record attributed the 2x and 2.6x figures to OpenBLAS; on the page they are against BLASFEO and BLIS respectively. MIT license, 18 stars and last commit 2022-04-08 are confirmed; the README is titled LibShalom.

tier_reason: arXiv paper with no venue stated and no code; it gives GCC 7.5 on Kunpeng920 but no flags. That is first-party numbers with partial methodology, so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: SGEMM_NN (M=N=K<=80): on average 1.81x, 2.3x and 20.17x faster than OpenBLAS, ARMPL and BLIS respectively; DGEMM up to 1.48x vs OpenBLAS, 1.66x vs ARMPL, 15.0x vs BLIS; CGEMM/ZGEMM 9.6-13.68x vs BLIS
corrections.caveats: Paper only, no code repo; flags unstated; the large ratios over BLIS reflect BLIS lacking a small-GEMM path at the time; Kunpeng920 only

notes: The record misread the ratios as three transpose variants versus OpenBLAS; the paper attributes 1.81x, 2.3x and 20.17x to OpenBLAS, ARMPL and BLIS respectively.
